title: Why does Britain still own a rock in Spain?

post.caption: The World's Chokepoints: the Strait of Gibraltar. Tariq ibn Ziyad (711), the capture of 1704 and the Treaty of Utrecht (1713), the Great Siege (1779-83), the 1967 and 2002 referendums, and the 2026 UK-EU treaty. Images: public domain (incl. NASA). Map data: Natural Earth.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why does Britain still own a rock in Spain?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Gibraltar. A British territory at the gate between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Where exactly is it?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: At the southern tip of Spain. Here, Europe and Africa are only about fourteen kilometres apart.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: From space, the two continents almost touch.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Where does the name come from?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 711, the commander Tariq ibn Ziyad landed here with an army. The rock became Jabal Tariq, Tariq's mountain: Gibraltar.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So how did Britain get it?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1704, an English and Dutch fleet captured it in a war over the Spanish throne. In 1713, Spain signed it over to Britain.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Did Spain try to take it back?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Many times. The Great Siege lasted almost four years. Spain's floating gun batteries were set on fire, and the rock held.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: What do the people of Gibraltar want?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1967, they voted to stay British: twelve thousand one hundred and thirty-eight to forty-four. Two years later, Spain closed the border.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 2002, ninety-nine percent rejected sharing sovereignty with Spain.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And after Brexit?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In July 2026, Britain and the European Union signed a treaty. Routine checks at the Spanish border ended, and Gibraltar stays British.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why does the strait matter so much?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Every ship between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean passes here. Even the ocean does: Atlantic water pours in to refill a sea that evaporates.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: That's the last of the world's chokepoints. Like the video and follow History Sketches.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And tell us in the comments which one surprised you most!
